chapter: Picnics, wagon advertising and saloon work
title: Crowds, saloons and drinks
summary: The crowd reaction to the wagon band, whether musicians drank, and the prices and kinds of beer and liquor sold at halls.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: What about the people? What were they doing when you stopped?
Were they listening to have to see?

Oh, see, the people, when we stopped, they was near where we stopped at. They'd get to run out their houses there, get on the street, and started dancing, and all the fellas out the saloon, and it sounded so good to some of them guys in the saloon, and say, come on band, play another one, come on out and get a drink. They'd go out, get a drink, then they'd play another number for them. Like that.
Didn't any of the musicians drink?
Didn't any of the musicians drink? All of them drank.
All of them drank I knew of.
At the hall that you were speaking of, you know, that you were advertising with the Crescent Band, what did they serve there to drink?
Oh, well, they had, during that time they had, they sell their beer by the Cakes, Cakes beer. Oh, they had all kinds of whiskey, gin, everything.
Did they sell it by the glass? Oh yeah, by the glass. What kind of glasses?

Oh, the beer was a small little bit of glass like that. A little small, I don't know what you'd call that kind of glass. Regular tunk? A little handle on it, but a small glass. Oh yeah, it had a handle on it. So it's fine. Yeah, that's it. How much a glass?
Did they have barrels in those places? Sure. Other than the beer kegs?
Beer out of barrels. And what else would they have in the barrels?
Just beer, would it be wine or what?
Well, no, mostly beer in the barrels, but they had wines there, and they're wine by Quartz. Wines and the whiskeys and all like gills and things.
